paper.title: Large Engagement Networks for Classifying Coordinated Campaigns and Organic Twitter Trends
paper.venue: Proceedings of the Nineteenth International AAAI Conference on Web and Social Media (ICWSM 2025), 19(1): 688-702
paper.version: AAAI/OJS official PDF, metadata creationDate 2025-06-07; arXiv:2503.00599v2 used for version cross-check
paper.page_convention: 1-based PDF page numbers; PDF p.1 corresponds to printed page 688

claims.claim: LEN is a large Twitter engagement-network graph classification benchmark with 314 graphs in the official PDF: 179 campaigns and 135 non-campaigns.

evidence.note: Reports 179 campaign graphs, 135 non-campaign graphs, node and edge ranges, and subtype descriptions.
Compares LEN Original: 314 graphs, 11,769.23 average nodes, 23,593.97 average edges.
Defines LEN-small as 100 smallest networks, 51 campaign and 49 non-campaign.

caveats: Official data page and README snapshot report 170 campaigns and 135 non-campaigns, creating a 305-vs-314 version conflict.

claims.claim: The campaign label is topic-level campaign/non-campaign supervision derived from ephemeral astroturfing detection and manual trend curation, not a harmful-intent gold label.

evidence.note: Campaign topics are detected via lexicon-tweet ephemeral astroturfing and then filtered/annotated.
Non-campaign labels are manually curated from external/internal events and popular trends.
Authors warn it is unfair to label all campaigns as fully inauthentic or to disregard movements using a trained classifier.

caveats: Campaign detection depends on prior ephemeral astroturfing detector assumptions and a Turkey 2023 collection setting.
Non-campaign is a conservative organic-trend proxy, not proof of no coordination.

claims.claim: The paper provides moderate evidence that graph and spectral classifiers can separate campaign from non-campaign networks, with performance lower on the full large-graph LEN than on LEN-small.

evidence.note: LEN-small best accuracy 0.900 and F1 0.884 for GraphSAGE; full LEN best accuracy 0.747 for VNGE and best F1 0.788 for LSD.
LEN-small ROC/AUROC curves for multiple models.
Full LEN ROC/AUROC curves for multiple models.

caveats: The reported split is stratified random graph-level 75/25; no cross-time, cross-campaign-family, cross-platform, or leave-event-out test is reported.
The code snapshot appears to repeat five seeds on one split loaded before the seed loop.

claims.claim: Campaign type classification is substantially weaker than binary campaign-vs-non-campaign classification, especially by macro-F1.

evidence.note: Full LEN campaign type macro-F1 peaks at 0.383 for VNGE; LEN-small macro-F1 peaks at 0.671 for VNGE.
Confusion matrices show many predictions concentrated in Politics/Reform.
Authors attribute lower macro-F1 to imbalanced labels and state the type task is more challenging.

caveats: Campaign type labels such as Politics, Reform, Finance, Cult, and Noise are not harmfulness labels.
Small class counts make macro-F1 unstable.

claims.claim: Graph construction and implementation choices create notable reproducibility and leakage risks.

evidence.note: Repeated user-pair interactions are reduced to latest engagement, retaining about 74% of edges.
Twitter API restrictions make real-time detection and dataset extension infeasible or costly.
Random split is created before the seed loop; validation loss is commented out; five runs may vary initialization/training but not split.
Requirements contain incomplete pins such as scikit-learn== and pytorch-geometric=2.2.0.

caveats: This is an audit inference from source and code; exact released data files were not downloaded due size/access constraints.

claims.claim: LEN should not be cited as a unified Harmfulness SOTA or as a coordination-discovery method.

evidence.note: The task is graph classification to distinguish campaigns from organic trends.
Potentially negative social impacts are mentioned as motivation, not as a labeled harmfulness outcome.
Authors explicitly warn against overusing campaign labels to disregard movements as inauthentic.

caveats: The dataset can be useful as a coordination-characterization benchmark, but harmfulness requires separate annotation and validation.
